basis: Intellectual disability, leukoencephalopathy and objective myopathy define the syndrome. Dental caries is a separate disease; oral dysmorphism alone does not establish damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: caries occurs in 30-79% but is a separately diagnosed dental disease; narrow mouth and palate do not establish functional injury.

basis: Autoimmune panuveitis with diagnostic meningeal inflammation; persistent skin/hair pigment loss occurs in 80-99%. Hearing loss (30-79%) omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: meningeal inflammation is a major diagnostic domain; CSF pleocytosis and cognitive impairment are annotated at 80-99%.

basis: Renal dysfunction and secondary PTH excess define disease; sustained PTH-mediated abnormal bone turnover and bone loss affect approximately 30% or more.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: chronic PTH excess directly causes high-turnover skeletal injury in approximately 30% or more; this is an intrinsic endocrine effect.

basis: B-cell/antibody deficiency defines disease. Sparse cytopenia reports do not establish direct hematologic injury independent of separately reported leukemia.

decisions.haematologic: none: anemia (1/1) and pancytopenia (1/2) meet numerical thresholds, but direct injury independent of leukemia or its treatment is unestablished.

basis: Corticospinal tract degeneration defines disease; bladder sphincter loss of function occurs in 30-79%. Secondary pes cavus does not establish direct skeletal injury.

decisions.renal: involved: urinary bladder sphincter dysfunction is documented functional loss in 30-79%, rather than a later risk of urinary disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: pes cavus (30-79%) reflects secondary motor imbalance; direct skeletal damage is not established by the foot-shape finding.

basis: Subcutaneous fat loss and metabolic dysfunction define disease. Steatosis/hepatomegaly (30-79%) do not establish functional liver injury; hypertension is separately diagnosed.

decisions.hepatic: none: steatosis/hepatomegaly occurs in 30-79%, but separately diagnosed fatty liver and lipid deposition alone do not establish qualifying functional damage.

basis: Immunodeficiency with anemia 3/3, leukopenia 2/3 and hypocellular marrow 1/1; otosclerosis and conductive hearing loss 2/2. Cholangitis is a separately diagnosed infection.

decisions.haematologic: involved: anemia 3/3, leukopenia 2/3 and marrow hypocellularity 1/1 support direct blood/marrow involvement beyond isolated immune-cell deficiency.
decisions.hepatic: none: cholangitis (3/3) is a separately diagnosed infectious complication; independent chronic hepatic injury is not established.

basis: Anterior horn/lower motor neuron disease; persistent distal upper-limb muscle wasting in 80-99% represents actual muscle tissue loss, beyond weakness alone.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: defining persistent amyotrophy occurs in 80-99%; denervation causes actual muscle tissue loss as part of this disease.

basis: Explicitly nonsyndromic brain overgrowth. The accompanying multisystem HPO profile conflicts with the isolated definition and cannot establish extracerebral involvement.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: atrial septal defect (30-79%) conflicts with the explicitly isolated concept and appears to reflect syndromic annotation.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: delayed skeletal maturation (80-99%) and genu valgum (30-79%) belong to a conflicting syndromic profile, not established isolated megalencephaly.

basis: Cerebral vascular amyloid deposition and neurodegeneration define disease; early cataracts and progressive hearing loss occur in most classically affected patients.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: ITM2B-related cerebral amyloid deposition is not, by itself, an endocrine disease or an established inborn metabolic disorder.
decisions.otologic: involved: progressive sensorineural hearing loss is a characteristic manifestation in most affected patients over the typical course.
